entities.summary: Pope Anastasius IV, born Corrado Demetri della Suburra, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 8 July 1153 to his death in 1154. He is the most recent pope to take the name "Anastasius" upon his election. Anastasius IV was born in Rome, Italy, around 1100-1110, but the exact date is unknown. He was a member of the noble family of the Suburra and married a woman named Alberada de Lancia. Anastasius IV succeeded Pope Adrian IV, who died on 1 July 1154, and was elected pope on 8 July 1153. He reigned for only one year, until his death on 10 December 1154. Anastasius IV played a significant role in the politics of the Catholic Church during the 12th century, and his papacy was marked by several key events, including the election of a new pope and the succession of the Holy Roman Emperor. Anastasius IV's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the grandeur and the controversies of the Catholic Church during this period.
